prompt: When asked to choose between a life without work and working most of the time, people would always choose not to work. Do you agree or disagree?
essay:
Many people dream of having enough financial security to stop working altogether. Consequently, some argue that, if given the choice, everyone would prefer a life free from work rather than spending most of their time working. While this may be true for those who find their jobs stressful or unrewarding, I disagree with the claim that people would *always* choose not to work.

It is understandable why some people would prefer a life without work. For many individuals, employment is primarily a means of earning a living rather than a source of personal fulfilment. Long working hours, demanding workloads, and workplace stress can leave employees with little time for family, hobbies, or relaxation. As a result, if financial concerns were removed, many would choose to devote more time to travelling, pursuing personal interests, or spending time with loved ones. Such a lifestyle could significantly improve both physical and mental well-being.

However, paid employment fulfils important psychological and social needs that leisure alone cannot fully satisfy. Beyond providing an income, meaningful work gives people a sense of purpose, achievement, and identity. For example, many doctors, teachers, and researchers continue working despite having sufficient financial resources because they value the opportunity to contribute to society and apply their expertise. Moreover, the workplace offers opportunities for social interaction, personal growth, and continuous learning, all of which help people maintain motivation and self-worth. Without these experiences, some individuals may eventually feel isolated or lack a clear sense of direction, even if they enjoy complete financial freedom.

In conclusion, although many people would welcome greater freedom from work, it is unrealistic to claim that everyone would choose not to work if given the opportunity. For many, meaningful employment represents far more than a source of income, making it an indispensable part of a fulfilling life.
